paper.central_claim: AgenticEval is a multi-agent framework that ingests unstructured policy documents into a structured testable knowledge base, generates a safety test suite and perpetually evolves it through an Evaluator-Analyst-Generator loop, uncovering vulnerabilities static benchmarks miss (e.g., GPT-5's EU AI Act safety rate drops from 72.50% to 36.36% over iterations).
paper.title: AgenticEval: Toward Agentic and Self-Evolving Safety Evaluation of Large Language Models

signatures.object: Testable knowledge base K*: hierarchical rule tree with per-atomic-rule explanation, compliant guidance G_should and adversarial guidance G_should_not
signatures.information: Regulation text (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, MAS FEAT), optional user template, web search results in the document's language
signatures.operation: Specialist agent recursively decomposes regulation to atomic rules then enriches each with search-grounded compliant/violating examples
signatures.output: K* used by Generator and Evaluator
signatures.feedback: None from targets at this stage
signatures.selection_rule: None; validated only by embedding-similarity heatmaps (Fig 2)
signatures.persistence: K* reused for every evaluated model
signatures.later_use: Source of test generation and judging rubrics
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o Structure raises GPT-5 NIST safety 64.29->75.40
signatures.failure_boundary: Technical interpretation of law, not legal judgment (authors)

signatures.object: Test suite {Q_r}^(k) (question groups per atomic rule) and attack strategy S_attack, evolved for K_max=3 rounds against one target model
signatures.information: Per-rule successful/failed responses R+ and R- of the target model, judged by the Evaluator
signatures.operation: Analyst.Refine -> analysis + attack strategy; Generator in 'refined' mode creates harder targeted tests; re-evaluate
signatures.output: Next-round suite; History of results; final safety report
signatures.feedback: LLM-judge binary verdict with rationale, rubric from K*
signatures.selection_rule: All generated tests accepted; no validity, dedup or difficulty-calibration gate described
signatures.persistence: History within a run; no cross-run or cross-target persistence
signatures.later_use: Only later rounds against the same target
signatures.claimed_effect: Safety rate declines over iterations; static variant 48.60 vs 36.36 (GPT-5, EU)
signatures.failure_boundary: Harder tests may be invalid/ambiguous; judge capability mismatch; higher cost

signatures.object: Evaluator agent (rubric judge, binary verdict + rationale)
signatures.information: Test case, question-specific criterion, rule guidance
signatures.feedback: Human audit of 100 random cases per framework

gap.author_gap: Static benchmarks suffer static lag, scope limitation and poor adaptability, leaving models deemed safe vulnerable to emerging threats and non-compliant with regulations.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible and specific for regulation-grounded evaluation; adaptive/self-evolving red-teaming (AutoDAN-Turbo, AutoRedTeamer, ALI-Agent) already exists, so the gap that remains is regulation ingestion plus evaluation reporting.
gap.lineage: HELM/DecodingTrust/StrongREJECT (static) -> COMPL-AI (manual EU AI Act codification) -> AutoDAN-Turbo/AutoRedTeamer/ALI-Agent (lifelong/adaptive) -> AgenticEval.
gap.residue: Not shown that regulation grounding adds value over adaptive red-teaming, or that evolved suites are valid and transferable.
gap.stakes: Compliance conclusions about frontier models rest on judged pass rates over a few dozen tests per category.
gap.method_response: Structured rule tree + grounded guidance + three-round failure-conditioned test refinement.
gap.remaining_gap: Test validity audit, cross-target transfer, static-benchmark comparison, cost accounting.
unresolved: Closest-neighbor evaluators were not run; no local copies pinned

claims.text: The self-evolving evaluation loop uncovers deeper vulnerabilities than static suites.
claims.setting: 3 regulations, 11 models, K_max=3, single run; GPT-5 EU AI Act 72.50 -> 36.36
claims.baseline_control: w/o Refine static variant (48.60 final); jailbreak baselines AutoDAN/PAIR/AutoDAN-Turbo (figure only)
claims.selection_vs_test: Tests are conditioned on the target's failures and scored on the same target
claims.result_denominator: Suite sizes not reported; implied per-category n~16-29
claims.allowed_conclusion: Failure-conditioned refinement lowers measured pass rates relative to the initial and static suites; that this reflects valid, transferable vulnerabilities is unproven.

claims.text: Each component (structure, enrichment, refinement) is necessary.
claims.setting: Ablations on GPT-5 (text numbers: NIST 64.29->75.40; EU 36.36->48.60)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Removing the components raises GPT-5's measured safety; other model/regulation bars not readable.

claims.text: The Evaluator agent's judgments are reliable.
claims.setting: 100 random cases per framework vs human annotation
claims.allowed_conclusion: Substantial agreement with human labels on the sampled cases; reliability on hardened rounds and against stronger targets is not separated.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Within-run, same-target adaptation; no cross-target or cross-run retention is evaluated, and the measured quantity is the evaluator's own pass-rate drop.
assessment.scope_note: In scope as evaluation_resource (evaluator/benchmark artifact evolved from execution feedback); retention is within-run only, so no retained-improvement claim is credited.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In a three-iteration, single-run protocol with GPT-4.1/Gemini-2.5-Pro agents, regulation-derived question groups plus an Analyst-driven refinement loop lower measured safety rates (GPT-5 EU AI Act 72.50->36.36; static variant 48.60) and the LLM judge agrees with humans on 88-91% of 100 sampled cases per framework; validity of hardened tests and transfer across targets are not shown.
unresolved: Test validity audit of evolved items
Comparison with an existing static regulation benchmark and with ALI-Agent/AutoRedTeamer

G.reason: Real limitation of static benchmarks, but nearest adaptive evaluators (ALI-Agent, AutoRedTeamer, AutoDAN-Turbo) already self-evolve; only the regulation-ingestion step is new and its marginal value over adaptive red-teaming is not isolated; COMPL-AI is not run.

M.reason: Concrete pipeline (rule tree + grounded guidance, question groups, rubric judge, Analyst->Generator loop) addresses the stated gap, but equating 'lower pass rate' with 'deeper vulnerability' is a weak assumption and no test-validity mechanism is provided.

X.reason: Roles, tools and models (MetaGPT; GPT-4.1/Gemini 2.5 Pro) are stated, K_max=3; missing are suite sizes, de-duplication/validity filtering of generated tests, what state the Analyst carries between rounds, and full prompts (high-level abstractions only).

E.measurement.reason: Judge is validated against 100 human-labelled cases per framework (acc 88-91%, kappa 0.77-0.81), which is more than most; however efficacy is defined as lower pass rate, hardened-test validity is never audited, and GPT-4.1 judges stronger targets.

E.causality.reason: Component ablations (w/o Structure, Enrich, Refine) and jailbreak baselines exist, but numbers are mostly in figures, the static variant's test count/compute is not matched, there is no random-regeneration control, and the drop is expected from adversarial conditioning on the target's own failures.

E.holdout.reason: Evolved tests are conditioned on the same target they are scored against; no check that suites evolved on one model expose weaknesses in others, no static-benchmark comparison, no contamination analysis; coverage of 3 regulations/11 models is the only breadth.

E.statistics.reason: Judge agreement reports kappa on n=100, but main safety rates have no intervals, seeds or repeats, and suite sizes are not stated (Table 1 values imply denominators of ~16-29 per category).

E.cost.reason: No call counts, tokens, dollars, latency or budget-matched comparison with static suites or jailbreak baselines were found; only a qualitative limitation sentence.

evidence.quote: However, existing static benchmarks are ill-equipped to address the dynamic nature of AI risks and evolving regulations, creating a critical safety gap.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap: static safety benchmarks lag evolving risks and regulations.

evidence.quote: : as fixed snapshots in time, they quickly become outdated when new attack vectors emerge or model capabilities evolve.
evidence.support_explanation: 'Static lag' limitation of static benchmarks; no static regulation benchmark is run as a baseline (COMPL-AI is only cited).

evidence.quote: employs an emulation-refinement pipeline to probe long-tail risks in human value alignment, yet it relies on general ethical categories rather than autonomously parsing and validating against unstructured regulatory texts.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest adaptive evaluator ALI-Agent is distinguished by regulation parsing, but not run as a baseline.

evidence.quote: maintains a memory-based portfolio of attacks that adapts continuously to emerging defenses.
evidence.support_explanation: AutoRedTeamer already accumulates attack knowledge across rounds; cited, not compared.

evidence.quote: Rather than merely cataloging failures, the Analyst agent learns the target model’s failure modes and synthesizes these insights into new directives, which in turn guide the Generator to craft more targeted test cases, transforming static audits into dynamic red-teaming.
evidence.support_explanation: Core self-evolving operation: failure analysis -> attack directives -> new tests.

evidence.quote: This sequence of analysis, refined generation, and re-evaluation constitutes the evolutionary evaluation loop, where insights from one round systematically inform the attack strategy for the next.
evidence.support_explanation: Loop description; no validity filter or acceptance rule for generated tests is described.

evidence.quote: ), as we found this number strikes an effective balance between uncovering vulnerabilities and managing computational costs for the models tested.
evidence.support_explanation: K_max=3 iterations across all experiments, chosen by the authors for cost balance; 'perpetual' evolution is therefore a three-round run per target.

evidence.quote: are powered by GPT-4.1, chosen for its strong analytical and logical reasoning capabilities.
evidence.support_explanation: Specialist, Evaluator and Analyst all use GPT-4.1; Generator uses Gemini 2.5 Pro; judge is not an independent model family from the guidance author.

evidence.quote: , calculated as the percentage of test cases successfully passed as determined by our Evaluator agent.
evidence.support_explanation: Safety Rate is judged by the Evaluator agent; no suite size is stated.
Per-category rates such as 68.75, 73.91, 84.21, 75.86 imply per-category denominators of roughly 16-29 test cases (our arithmetic: 11/16, 17/23, 16/19, 22/29).

evidence.quote: The results demonstrate a consistent decline in safety as the evaluation hardens. For instance, GPT-5 sees its safety rate against the EU AI Act fall sharply from 72.50% in the initial round to just 36.36% by the final iteration.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result; the authors attribute the drop directly to escalating difficulty.

evidence.quote: Lower scores indicate more effective evaluation and deeper vulnerability discovery.
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation efficacy is defined as a lower pass rate, which unfair or invalid tests could also produce.

evidence.quote: By forcing the Generator to condition on the entire document rather than atomic provisions, the system loses its ability to lock onto specific decision boundaries; empirically, this causes GPT-5’s apparent safety rate on the NIST AI RMF to surge from 64.29% to 75.40%.
evidence.support_explanation: Quantified ablation of the structuring step (GPT-5, NIST); other ablation bars are in Fig 4 only.

evidence.quote: This prevents the system from learning from model failures, significantly hampering its ability to uncover deep-seated vulnerabilities; for instance, on the EU AI Act, removing this loop causes GPT-5’s safety score to jump from 36.36% to 48.60%.
evidence.support_explanation: Static variant (no Analyst refinement) gives 48.60 vs 36.36; test counts for the variants are not stated.

evidence.quote: Notably, the full AgenticEval outperforms not only its ablated variants but also the strong jailbreaking baselines.
evidence.support_explanation: Comparison with AutoDAN, PAIR and AutoDAN-Turbo is reported only as bars in Fig 4.

evidence.quote: To assess its accuracy, we conducted a human-in-the-loop validation by randomly sampling 100 test cases per regulatory framework and manually annotating them to establish ground truth.
evidence.support_explanation: Judge validated on 100 random cases per framework; whether evolved-round cases are included is not stated.
NIST: accuracy 91.00, precision 89.13, recall 90.47, F1 89.79, kappa 0.81 (EU 88.33/0.77; MAS 89.67/0.79).

evidence.quote: The results clearly show distinct clusters of high similarity (darker colors) within these designated groups.
evidence.support_explanation: Specialist structuring is validated only by embedding-similarity heatmaps of the model's own explanation fields, not against human-extracted rules.

evidence.quote: Finally, the multi-step reasoning inherent in the Self-evolving Evaluation loop incurs higher computational costs and latency compared to static benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Cost acknowledged qualitatively; no numbers.

evidence.quote: Instances of hallucination or a capability mismatch, where the Evaluator Agent is less sophisticated than the target model, may occasionally lead to misclassified judgments, particularly when probing subtle adversarial nuances.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors acknowledge judge capability mismatch (GPT-4.1 judging GPT-5/Gemini-2.5-pro).

evidence.quote: are high-level abstractions, distilled to their essential logic for clarity and comprehensibility.
evidence.support_explanation: Released prompt descriptions are abstractions; full prompts are not in the material.

evidence.quote: Evaluating safety with isolated prompts is insufficient, as a model may pass a direct query but fail on a subtle variation.
evidence.support_explanation: Rationale for Question Groups (base, jailbreak, mcq/tf, multimodal facets per atomic rule).

evidence.quote: It then employs its integrated web search capability to retrieve a corpus of pertinent real-world examples, incidents, and discussions.
